articles.body: A guy on Hacker News installed the Flatpak build, opened his own web apps, his news sites, and Hacker News itself, then wrote that he was completely dumbfounded. He had been told for decades that building a new browser was like tilting at windmills. Every site he cared about rendered correctly. i spent an evening reading the 630 comments under that thread instead of doing my job. The reaction kept pulling me back, because it was not the usual cynical sneer. "This actually worked amazingly well," one person wrote. Another said it was sipping 53MB of memory with multiple tabs open. A third complained that scrolling felt slightly jerky. Ladybird shipped its first alpha on November 23, 2026. macOS and Linux only. Backed by a 501(c)(3) non-profit.

articles.title: 87 times the plan was wrong
articles.excerpt: In October one of us counted every acceptance note we wrote that month. There were 171. A script read each one and sorted out three things: did the build pass on the first try, did the build have a de…
articles.body: In October one of us counted every acceptance note we wrote that month. There were 171. A script read each one and sorted out three things: did the build pass on the first try, did the build have a defect, and did the plan itself turn out to be wrong. The plan was wrong 87 times. The build was wrong 9 times. That's almost ten to one. And not one of the 87 plan errors caused a rejection or a second build round. This post is about why both of those numbers can be true at once. How we work, in one paragraph Nothing here gets built straight from an idea. First a spec: what to build, what to measure, and what counts as done, written as numbered clauses. Then someone else builds it. Then the one who wrote the spec takes the finished thing and measures every clause herself.

articles.title: Resume Bullets That Show Impact: A Three-Part Rewrite You Can Do Tonight
articles.excerpt: Resume Bullets That Show Impact: A Three-Part Rewrite You Can Do Tonight Most resume bullets describe a job, not a person doing it. "Responsible for onboarding new clients" tells a reader what was on…
articles.body: Resume Bullets That Show Impact: A Three-Part Rewrite You Can Do Tonight Most resume bullets describe a job, not a person doing it. "Responsible for onboarding new clients" tells a reader what was on your list of duties. It does not tell them what happened because you were there. The good news is that this is a writing problem, and writing problems have repeatable fixes. You do not need a new career story. You need a better sentence shape and a short session with your own memory. The shape: action, specifics, result A bullet that shows impact usually has three parts: Action. A verb you can defend in an interview: built, rewrote, cut, trained, negotiated, organised, automated, documented. Specifics. What you worked on, and how big it was.

Upload a selfie and get two images: a collectible-style character card and a separate portrait for your profile picture. Choose art style, aspect ratio, card language, and 2K/4K output. Nothing to install, no account needed for the quiz, and answers stay in the browser. What I learned building it Prompt structure matters more than model choice for consistent character cards. articles.title: WARN Act and Your Utility Bills — What Happens to Your Lights, Heat, and Water After a Layoff Notice
articles.excerpt: A layoff notice is usually read as a jobs story. It is also a bills story. The 60 days of notice the WARN Act requires are meant to give you time to plan, and the utility bill is where that planning p…
articles.body: A layoff notice is usually read as a jobs story. It is also a bills story. The 60 days of notice the WARN Act requires are meant to give you time to plan, and the utility bill is where that planning pays off first: the protections that keep your heat and lights on are time-sensitive, and several only work if you ask before you fall behind. Layoff Atlas currently tracks 718 WARN notices covering 59,910 reported workers in the 90-day window — 23,701 in California and 16,261 in Washington. The heaviest upcoming week starts December 31, with 11,047 workers' jobs scheduled to end. These are reported plans, not confirmed job losses: some notices are later delayed, reduced, or withdrawn. But every worker named in one faces the same question — what happens to the bills while the paycheck stops?

articles.title: Orbital data centers are a cooling problem, not a solar problem
articles.excerpt: On 25 November 2026 the US Federal Communications Commission did something that would have sounded like science fiction a decade ago: it authorized SpaceX to deploy one million orbital compute modules…
articles.body: On 25 November 2026 the US Federal Communications Commission did something that would have sounded like science fiction a decade ago: it authorized SpaceX to deploy one million orbital compute modules — satellites whose job is to run computation in space and send the results back to Earth. The FCC called it the first authorization of its kind in US history. The application, filed in January, describes altitudes between 500 and 2,000 km, 30-degree and sun-synchronous inclinations, and orbital shells up to 50 km wide. Most of the coverage treated this as a story about abundant energy. That is only half of the engineering picture, and it is the half that is easiest to solve. The harder half is heat, latency, and the fact that a data center is not a static object.

articles.body: Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . articles.excerpt: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
